A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same T* research work. All pages, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A.1–A.2 are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original SDAR training and evaluation results, including benchmark accuracies, training trajectories, decoding statistics, and appendix case studies.

after.justification: V5 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Both versions alternate standard and half-block-shifted TraceRL updates, then double block size after each stage. V5 replaces the abstract SHIFT operation with explicit partition notation and implementation explanations; v3 already describes the same shifted-partition procedure.

E1.justification: Both use the same Openr1math training coverage, evaluate MATH500, GSM8K, and AIME24, and include the same mathematical decoding examples. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the original SDAR checkpoints and direct TraceRL baselines. Table 1 also retains Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen2.5-1.5B; comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 revises the stated direct-TraceRL budget from 30 epochs to 30 policy-update steps, and Figure 1's caption adopts update-step units. This changes the reported budget description without establishing that experiments were rerun. Model configurations, sampling settings, Pass@3 evaluation, and MATH500-based checkpoint selection remain otherwise unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the same training-stability analysis, block-size comparisons, LocalStrict/accuracy/TPF analysis, and decoding case studies in Figures 3–4. V5 adds explanatory qualifications but no new ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed counts, repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V5's expanded checkpoint-selection discussion introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2, plotted trajectories and benchmark curves, and appendix case-study outputs are unchanged. For example, both report T* at 1.7B and block size 8 as 63.40 on MATH500, 82.40 on GSM8K, and 7.78 on AIME24.

T1.justification: V5 adds explicit mathematical definitions of standard and shifted response partitions in Equations 5–7, including the initial short block and finite-length boundary handling. The existing objectives and LocalStrict definition remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces tentative convergence to an alternative schedule with block-specific nonmonotone decoding and explicitly asserts consistent superiority and greater stability over direct TraceRL. The central contribution remains progressive block scaling. The superiority wording is broader than Table 2's retained AIME24 tie of 6.66 at 1.7B, block size 16.

C2.justification: V5 explicitly warns that MATH500 results reflect checkpoint selection on that benchmark and emphasizes cross-benchmark consistency. It also qualifies TPF as a forward-pass proxy rather than a direct latency measurement, replacing v3's stronger throughput/latency inference. Existing cold-start and large-block limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 2.2 newly specifies response-only partitioning, fixed prompt context, boundary handling, and preservation of tokens and rewards during shifting. Section 3.1 elaborates periodic MATH500 selection and reuse of one checkpoint across benchmarks. Hardware, optimizer, learning rate, and sampling details are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works are unchanged. Both position T* as a TraceRL-based curriculum and internal schedule learning as complementary to external tree/graph reasoning methods.

P1.justification: V5 rewrites portions of the abstract, introduction, and conclusion, expands Section 2.2, gives checkpoint selection a separate paragraph, and standardizes stage/update terminology. Affiliations and acknowledgments are updated, while the main section sequence and much of the exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: Algorithm 1 is reformatted and relocated, and existing figures and tables shift with text reflow. Figure 1 gains an expanded caption specifying policy-update steps, although its axis still reads Training Epochs. The plotted content, table structures, and appendix displays are retained.

improvement.justification: V5 improves reproducibility through explicit partition definitions and improves interpretation by acknowledging MATH500 checkpoint-selection bias and distinguishing TPF from measured latency. These limited gains outweigh the remaining Figure 1 unit inconsistency and the abstract's overly broad superiority wording relative to the retained AIME24 tie. The empirical evidence itself is unchanged.
